newsitem.title: USA: WSCC board approves Pacific Intertie increase.
newsitem.headline: WSCC board approves Pacific Intertie increase.

text.p: The Western Systems Coordinating Council's (WSCC) Board of Trustees approved late Tuesday a plan to raise capacity on the Pacific Intertie to 6,250 megawatts (MW), the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said Wednesday.
The plan is now before WSCC's 91 member systems for their approval.
BPA has been seeking since November approval to raise the Intertie capacity, which has been capped at 5,200 MW out of a rated capacity of 7,900 MW, since last summer when two blackouts hit the West.
The "winter" plan to raise the limit to 6,250 MW was given to the entire WSCC membership on Monday, and they will have 10 working days to review it.

If the members approve the plan, the WSCC board will hold a teleconference March 21 to "reaffirm" their vote, but information on exactly when when the Intertie capacity would be raised was not available.
BPA's "spring" operating studies, which support raising the capacity to 7,800 MW where also discussed at Tuesday's board meeting, but no official actions were taken, the BPA spokeswoman said.

But a special WSCC study group is expected to present spring operating recommendations to the board on March 20 and a board meeting will be held April 24 to complete the process of "taking on a spring transfer limit," the BPA spokeswoman said.
